To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that a constitutive genetic reduction of ephrins in mice aggravates the phenotype and reduces survival without affecting disease initiation in a rodent ALS model, and that a reduction in ephrin-A protein levels is associated with a faster disease progression in patients.

we identified ephrin-A4 and ephrin-A3, members of the EphA4/ephrin-A system, as modifiers of disease progression in a murine model for ALS and in humans, and that we identified ephin-A5 to aggravate disease progression in a model of ALS and in humans.

(i) EphA4 is a disease-modifying gene for ALS, (ii) EphA4 ligand ephrin-A1 and EphA4 receptor are upregulated in the spinal cord and brain of ALS patients, and (iii) EphA4 receptor is required for the survival of motor neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genetic modifiers of ALS and the characterization of their role in the disease.
the identification of disease modifiers that might help to improve ALS therapy.
the role of Eph-ephrins in the pathophysiological mechanisms of ALS, and their potential as therapeutic target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EphA4 is an ALS disease-modifier and ephrin-A ligand is a disease-modifier of progression.
the role of Eph-ephrins in ALS is complex, and that their contribution to the pathophysiology and the clinical course of ALS is multifactorial.
ephrin-A1 and A5 are disease modifying factors that accelerate disease progression in ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Eph-ephin system might play an important role in the later stage of disease progression and that the balance between EphA4 and ephrin-A ligands might determine the outcome of the disease in the later stage.

the Eph-ephirn system is an important regulator of the motor neuron system during development and in adulthood, and that a deregulation of this system might play a role during the pathophysiology and disease progression of ALS.
EphA4 and ephrin-A4 are disease modifiers for ALS, whereas EphA4 ligand ephrin-A2 is a disease driver for ALS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Eph-ephrins might be a promising target in ALS.
the Eph-epharin system might be a potential target for the treatment of motor neuron diseases.
the Eph-ephirn system plays a role in ALS and that different members of this system can have different effects on disease onset, disease progression and disease severity.
